instructions: Peel one of the onions and cut it in half. Put it in a large pot with the 1 1/4 lb chicken, the 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp of the salt, 1/2 tsp of the black pepper and 5 cups water.

Bring it to a boil over high heat, then turn it down to medium low so it bubbles gently. Skim off any foam and simmer for 25 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut into it: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear and leave it to drain. Finely chop the second onion.

Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium. Add the 1/4 cup cashews, 1/4 cup almonds and 2 tbsp pine nuts and stir for 3 to 5 minutes, until they're golden brown. Keep an eye on the pine nuts. They darken first. Transfer the nuts onto a plate.
Melt the remaining 2 tbsp butter in the same pot, add the chopped onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft.

Turn the heat up to medium high and add the 1/2 lb beef with 1/2 tsp of the salt. Break it up with a spoon and leave it alone for a minute between stirs. After 5 to 6 minutes there's no pink left and the bits are starting to brown.
Stir in the 2 tsp seven spice and the last 1/4 tsp black pepper and cook for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant.
When the chicken is done, lift it onto a board. Pour the cooking liquid through a sieve into a large measuring cup or bowl.

Add the drained rice to the beef and stir for 1 minute, until every grain is coated. Pour in 2 1/4 cups of the cooking liquid and the last 1/2 tsp salt and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes. No peeking.
While the rice cooks, shred the chicken with two forks and toss it with 1/4 cup of the leftover cooking liquid so it stays moist. Cover it to keep it warm. Save the rest of the liquid for a soup.
Fluff the rice with a fork and spoon it onto a platter. Pile the chicken on top and scatter the nuts over it.
Chop a small handful of the parsley and scatter it over the platter.
Taste the rice. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
method_notes: Both versions poach the chicken with onion, cinnamon sticks and bay leaves, cook the rice in that broth with onion and ground beef, and finish it with chicken and butter-toasted almonds, cashews and pine nuts on top. Feel Good Foodie poaches thighs for 25 minutes, seasons the beef with seven spice only, and spoons it onto a platter; The Matbakh boils a whole chicken for an hour and a half, adds allspice, cinnamon and nutmeg, and layers the chicken and rice in a bowl to turn out as a dome. This one follows Feel Good Foodie's thighs, spices and platter.
